# SK3002 — Blocking on an async call

<!-- Generated from Rules/Rikarin.Skala.Rules.Metadata/rules.json. Do not edit. -->

`.Result`, `.Wait()` or `.GetAwaiter().GetResult()` on a `Task` or `ValueTask`.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | Async |
| Default severity | warning |
| Scope | Semantic |
| Needs a compilation | yes |
| Fix | yes, review it |
| Language version floor | — |
| Since | 0.8 |

## Why

Blocking a thread on a task is the classic ASP.NET and WPF deadlock: the continuation needs the synchronization context the blocked thread is holding, and neither side moves again. Even where it does not deadlock it consumes a pool thread for the duration, which under load is how a server stops responding to anything at all. It also re-wraps the exception in an `AggregateException`, so the `catch` a reader expects to fire does not. `await` does none of these things.

## Example

Instead of:

```csharp
async Task<int> LoadAsync() {
    var text = File.ReadAllTextAsync(path).Result;
    return text.Length;
}
```

Write:

```csharp
async Task<int> LoadAsync() {
    var text = await File.ReadAllTextAsync(path);
    return text.Length;
}
```

## When it does not fire

The rule fires only when the receiver's type is `System.Threading.Tasks.Task`, `Task<T>`, `ValueTask` or `ValueTask<T>` as resolved by the semantic model — never on a `.Result` property of a user type that happens to be called that, and never when the type did not resolve. It is silent wherever `await` is unavailable or wrong: an entry point, a constructor, a finalizer, an operator, a property or field initializer, a `lock` body, an `unsafe` context, an expression tree, a query clause, and inside test code, where blocking is deliberate. ⚠ **Test code is decided by the enclosing method's attribute *or* by the enclosing type holding a test case** ([#319], [#303]) — xUnit gives a test class no attribute to read, so a fixture constructor, an `IDisposable.Dispose` teardown and a field initializer inside a real test class carry nothing of their own and were all reported. ⚠ **A helper in a *separate* class is still reported, and that is a refusal rather than an oversight.** Reaching it needs a call graph, or the compilation-references test #303 examined and refused — refused for a measured reason, since the fixture harness gives every fixture the test host's whole assembly closure, and wiring it in turned 31 positive fixtures across six rules silent in one run. A fix is offered only where the enclosing method or lambda is *already* `async` and the expression is not inside a `lock`, which is where the rewrite is provably correct; elsewhere the finding is reported with no fix, because making a method `async` changes its signature and therefore its callers, which is not an edit a tool may apply unreviewed.
